material_composition.name: Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET)
properties: Good thermal stability (operating range from -60°C to 220°C)

environmental_impact.degradation_time: Up to 450 years in natural environments
environmental_concerns: Production contributes to significant greenhouse gas emissions
The synthesis process involves toxic petrochemicals
Limited biodegradability leads to persistent plastic pollution
Potential for leaching harmful chemicals into the environment during degradation

applications: Textiles (used in polyester fibers and clothing)

recycling.potential: High - PET is one of the most recyclable plastics available today.
methods: Enzymatic recycling (using enzymes to break down PET into its building blocks)
challenges: Contamination of PET with other materials complicates recycling
Limited recycling infrastructure in certain regions
Degradation of material properties with repeated recycling cycles
Need for public education on proper recycling practices

alternatives.name: Biodegradable Plastics (PLA)
alternatives.description: Polylactic Acid (PLA) is derived from renewable resources like corn starch, making it compostable under industrial conditions.
alternatives.sustainability_advantage: Does not contribute to long-term plastic pollution and is compostable, reducing waste impact.

alternatives.name: Glass
alternatives.description: A durable, non-toxic material that can be recycled indefinitely without loss of quality.
alternatives.sustainability_advantage: Lower environmental impact when produced sustainably, as glass can be recycled infinitely.

alternatives.name: Aluminum
alternatives.description: A lightweight and highly recyclable material used extensively for beverage cans and packaging.
alternatives.sustainability_advantage: Recycling aluminum saves about 90% of the energy required to produce new aluminum.

alternatives.name: Hemp Plastic
alternatives.description: Plastics made from hemp are biodegradable and can decompose faster than conventional plastics.
alternatives.sustainability_advantage: Biodegradable and sourced from a renewable resource, reducing dependence on fossil fuels.
